summary: Sparse triangular solver: forward substitution pass over rows 0..a4-1 followed by a backward substitution pass from row a4-2 down to 0. Row metadata is reached through two pointer arrays on this (this+0x0 for the forward pass, this+0x4 for the backward pass); each row subtracts the contributions of its nonzero off-diagonal entries (stored as byte-index/double pairs) from the workspace, then divides by the diagonal. The reciprocal uses the read-only constant dbl_59E420 (1.0). Called by sub_56ECF0 (0x0056ECF0) on the per-frame path.

local_names.this: solver handle holding the two sparse row-metadata arrays
local_names.a2: index/workspace array of double values addressed by row-entry byte indices
local_names.a3: current-column workspace cursor used as the right-hand side
local_names.v8: workspace index of the current row
local_names.v11: reciprocal of the diagonal value for the current row

operations.description: Forward substitution pass is gated on a4 > 0 (matrix dimension must be positive).
Forward pass iterates rows 0..a4-1, walking each row's metadata block through the pointer array at *this (this+0x0) plus a byte cursor.

For each row whose nonzero-count byte (at row metadata +1) is non-zero, subtracts the scaled contributions of its off-diagonal entries: workspace[row] -= coefficient * value for each (index, value) entry.
Computes the diagonal reciprocal v11 = 1.0 / workspace[row], with the 1.0 numerator sourced from the read-only constant dbl_59E420.
Normalizes the row's remaining off-diagonal entries: writes v11 * workspace[entry] back into the workspace at each entry's double slot.
Divides the current row's right-hand-side cursor value by the diagonal: workspace cursor = v11 * workspace cursor.
Backward substitution pass iterates i = a4-2 down to 0, walking row metadata through this[1] (this+0x4).
Backward pass subtracts the scaled contributions of each processed row's off-diagonal entries from the workspace cursor.
Returns the final byte-cursor result (the value of the last substitution operation).
Invoked by sub_56ECF0 (0x0056ECF0), the only recorded caller, on the per-frame path.
